backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP solve, repeatedly perturb the best packing's centres with Gaussian noise (sd about 0.03 to 0.05), re-run SLSQP, and keep the result only if the radius sum improves. Keep the time budget and repair step.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best packing

backlog.spec: Initialise centres on a jittered hexagonal or square-ish grid with n points spread over [0.1, 0.9]^2, using rng for jitter, and small equal radii. Use it for a fraction of restarts, with uniform random starts for the rest.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-like lattice initialisation

backlog.spec: Phase one optimises only the centres with all radii fixed to a common value found by bisection so the packing is feasible. Phase two releases the radii and runs SLSQP from that feasible point.
backlog.title: Two-phase equal-radius start

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 so SLSQP can reach a true local optimum rather than stopping early. Keep random restarts and the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Raise SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: Scale the objective by 1/n and the distance constraints so gradients are order one. This improves SLSQP line-search behaviour and reduces premature termination.
backlog.title: Objective and constraint scaling

backlog.spec: Pass analytic Jacobians for the objective and the constraint vector (pair distance derivatives with respect to centres and radii) via the jac argument. This removes finite-difference cost so more restarts fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Only include pair constraints for circle pairs whose centres are closer than the sum of radii plus a margin (for example 0.3), recomputed after each restart. This shrinks the constraint vector and speeds SLSQP.
backlog.title: Sparse constraint pairs

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, polish the best packing with scipy trust-constr using the same constraints, keeping whichever result has the larger radius sum. Adds a second local optimiser on the best candidate only.
backlog.title: Trust-constr fallback polish

backlog.spec: After repair, greedily grow each radius in random order to the largest value that keeps it feasible against walls and other circles, then repeat over circles until no radius increases. Recovers slack lost by the repair shrinkage.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth post-step

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative max-overlap repair with a single pass that sets each radius to the minimum of wall distance and half the distance to every other circle's contact limit, processed in order. This keeps more radius than uniform pairwise scaling.
backlog.title: Replace fixed shrink with exact repair

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK from 1e-9 to 1e-12 and verify validity with a tolerance-aware check, since the harness allows 1e-10 slack. Recovers a tiny amount of radius per circle.
backlog.title: Remove the 1e-9 shrink margin carefully

backlog.spec: Take the best packing, pick one or two circles at random, remove them, and reinsert them at the largest hole found by sampling random points, then re-optimise. Accept if the radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-repair local search on radii

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii from a skewed distribution (for example a random mix of large and small values) rather than a constant 0.05, so SLSQP starts with a varied size profile that better matches optimal packings.
backlog.title: Biased initial radii

backlog.spec: Place a fixed fraction of initial centres near the square's corners and edges, with the rest uniform, to encourage boundary-hugging configurations typical of good circle packings.
backlog.title: Corner and edge seeding

backlog.spec: Allocate restarts in two tiers: many cheap restarts with a low iteration cap, then the top few re-optimised with a high cap. This spends the budget on promising basins.
backlog.title: Time-split restarts with more diversity

backlog.spec: Track the best radius sum across restarts and stop random sampling after a long stagnation window, switching to basin hopping from the incumbent for the remaining time.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart budget by stagnation

backlog.spec: Keep the top k packings. Build new starts by taking the left half of one packing and the right half of another, cut at a random vertical line, then fill missing circles uniformly and optimise.
backlog.title: Elite pool with recombination

backlog.spec: Generate some starts with a mirror symmetry about the diagonal or a vertical axis by optimising half the circles and mirroring them. Symmetric starts often lead to strong packings.
backlog.title: Symmetry-based starts

backlog.spec: Add a small positive lower bound on each radius (for example 1e-3) in the SLSQP bounds to avoid degenerate zero-radius circles and improve conditioning.
backlog.title: Radius lower bound during optimisation

backlog.spec: Move the wall constraints into the SLSQP bounds on the centre coordinates (bounds of r to 1 minus r is not separable, so use the box [0,1] on centres) and keep only pair constraints, reducing constraint count.
backlog.title: Bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: Use the current best packing as the initial point for later restarts, with small random noise on centres and radii, rather than fresh uniform samples. Keeps good structure while exploring nearby.
backlog.title: Warm-start from incumbent with noise

backlog.spec: Precompute pair index arrays and compute the constraint vector with vectorised numpy only, avoiding repeated triu index construction. Cuts per-iteration overhead so more SLSQP iterations fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Vectorised constraint evaluation

backlog.spec: Pass SLSQP ftol around 1e-12 and a larger maxiter, and check result feasibility before accepting a restart. Ensures local optima are tightly converged.
backlog.title: Stop SLSQP on tolerance

backlog.spec: Derive per-restart seeds from the master seed with a SeedSequence spawn so restarts are independent and reproducible, rather than sharing one generator state.
backlog.title: Random restart seed diversity check

backlog.spec: Within one solve call, run the restart loop in fixed-size batches and keep the best of each batch, reducing variance from unlucky initial points.
backlog.title: Repeated-run ensemble averaging of starts

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty pulling centres toward the square centre during early SLSQP iterations, then remove it for the final stage. Helps the optimiser spread circles evenly before tightening.
backlog.title: Light centre regularisation

backlog.spec: When comparing packings with nearly equal radius sums, prefer the one with larger minimum pairwise slack, which tends to give more room for later polishing.
backlog.title: Radius-sum tie breaking by spread

backlog.spec: Start with a small initial radius and gradually increase the radius penalty weight over the first SLSQP calls, a continuation scheme that avoids early jamming.
backlog.title: Annealed initial radius scale

backlog.spec: Generate many cheap random configurations, score each by a quick penalty energy minimisation, and run full SLSQP only on the lowest-energy few. This filters out poor starts cheaply.
backlog.title: Multi-start from best-of-k initial configurations

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep a current packing separate from the best packing. Accept a new local optimum with probability min(1, exp((sum_new - sum_cur) / T)) instead of accepting only improvements, with T starting near 0.01 and decaying geometrically to about 1e-4 over the hopping phase. Always store the best packing seen, and return that one. Keep the hop as the existing Gaussian centre jitter with HOP_SD. Use rng for the acceptance draws so the result depends only on seed.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(w_i * r_i), where w is drawn once per call from rng uniform on [0.8, 1.2] for each circle. The constraints stay unchanged. This tilts each local solve toward different radius allocations, so it reaches different contact graphs from the same start. Every candidate is still scored by its true unweighted sum after repair, so selection is unchanged. Pass the rng or a seed into _solve_once.
backlog.title: Random per-circle objective weights in SLSQP

backlog.spec: Rewrite the pairwise constraint in _solve_once without the square root: use (cx_i - cx_j)^2 + (cy_i - cy_j)^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0 for each pair, and keep r_i + r_j >= 0 handled by the existing bounds. The constraint is smooth at zero distance and its gradients are simpler. Keep the wall constraints as they are. Then run the existing repair step on the result, so validity is still guaranteed by the harness check.
backlog.title: Squared-distance non-overlap constraints

backlog.spec: Add a move to the basin-hopping phase. Pick the circle with the smallest radius in the best packing, remove it, and sample 500 random points. Place the circle at the sample that maximises the distance to all other centres and walls (largest empty hole, approximated by the min over distance to other centres minus their radii, and distance to walls). Then run _solve_once from that configuration, followed by repair. Keep this move with probability 0.5 and use the usual Gaussian jitter otherwise.
backlog.title: Vacancy move: relocate the smallest circle

backlog.spec: After _solve_once and before repair, identify the active contacts: pairs whose gap is below 1e-6 and walls where the centre is within 1e-6 of the wall plus its radius. Form the system of equalities for those active contacts in the unknowns (centres and radii). Solve it with a few Gauss-Newton steps (least squares via numpy.linalg.lstsq), starting from the SLSQP solution, and accept the step only if the sum of radii rises and the constraints still hold to 1e-9. This gives a much tighter local optimum than SLSQP's default tolerance, and repair then removes any remaining tiny overlap.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call, run a short augmented-Lagrangian method on the same variables. Keep multipliers for the pair and wall constraints, and use the objective -sum(r) plus a quadratic penalty on constraint violations with weight rho starting at 10 and multiplied by 4 each outer step for about 5 steps. Each inner solve is an L-BFGS-B call on the unconstrained augmented Lagrangian. Use the output as the start for SLSQP. The penalty stage should move the start into a feasible region faster and with fewer SLSQP iterations, so the same time budget covers more starts.
backlog.title: Augmented-Lagrangian penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the cheap _relax energy for the start generation with a stochastic compression. Begin with all radii at 0.5 times the target r0 = 0.5/sqrt(n), and for about 2000 sweeps, propose a random displacement of each centre with a step that shrinks over time. Accept a move only if no overlap appears with the current radii, where radii are then grown a little for each circle to the largest value that keeps it clear of the others and walls. This gives a jammed start that is already nearly packed and has varied radii. Pass the resulting centres into _solve_once as the start.
backlog.title: Monte Carlo compression of random starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, instead of jittering all centres, choose a random disc of radius 0.25 in the unit square. Freeze all circles whose centres are outside it, and re-optimise only the circles inside it using SLSQP with the frozen circles included as fixed obstacles in the constraints. Then run a full _solve_once on the complete configuration from that start with a small jitter. Accept the new packing only if its radius sum improves on the best. This focuses the search on local defects in the packing rather than on global noise.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood re-optimisation of a window

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw rng.uniform(INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW, 2 * n) in the restart pool with a scrambled Halton sequence in two dimensions, generated with bases 2 and 3 in a loop over the index. Use a random offset and a per-seed digit permutation from rng so each seed differs. Map the points into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. Each start then covers the square more evenly than independent uniform draws. The rest of the restart pipeline is unchanged, and the pool still uses the cheap relaxation step to choose the best starts.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Halton starts

backlog.spec: Add a swap move to the basin-hopping phase. Pick two circles at random whose radii differ by more than 20 percent, exchange their centres, keep each radius attached to its index, and then run _solve_once on the swapped configuration with a small jitter. Radius-centre swaps of this kind move large circles into the slots left by small ones, which random Gaussian jitter rarely does. Keep the swap with probability 0.3 and use the normal jitter otherwise. Accept only if the best packing improves.
backlog.title: Random swap of circles of different sizes

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre draws in the restart pool with farthest-point sampling. For each start, draw 2000 uniform candidate points in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 with rng, then greedily pick the candidate that maximises its minimum distance to the points already chosen, until n centres are picked. Then pass these centres through the existing _relax and pool-selection code unchanged. Keep the rest of the restart loop and the basin-hopping phase as they are, and use only rng for randomness.
backlog.title: Max-min (farthest-point) sampled restart starts

backlog.spec: Before the restart phase, solve the (n-1)-circle problem with a short version of the existing pipeline, using about 15% of the restart budget. Take its best packing and insert the missing circle at the largest empty spot, found by evaluating the distance-to-nearest-centre-and-wall on a 100x100 grid. Set that circle's radius to the grid value. Then run _solve_once on the n-circle start, followed by the usual clip and _repair, and add the result to the candidate pool. Use only the seed for randomness.
backlog.title: Grow from an (n-1)-circle packing

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep HOP_SD as a variable instead of a constant. Track the acceptance rate of the last 20 hops, where a hop is accepted if it improves the best sum. If the rate is above 0.3, multiply HOP_SD by 1.2. If it is below 0.1, multiply by 0.8. Clamp HOP_SD to [0.005, 0.1]. Keep the 40% switch point and everything else the same.
backlog.title: Adaptive basin-hopping step size

backlog.spec: Run the restart phase in rungs. Start with the 20 pooled relaxed starts and run a cheap SLSQP with MAX_ITER=40 on each. Keep the best 5 by sum of radii after repair. Then restart the best 5 from their current iterates with MAX_ITER=200 and keep the best overall. Stop each rung when the rung's time share runs out. Use the same time split as now, so the total CPU budget stays at 80% of time_limit.
backlog.title: Successive halving over restart starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, generate K=4 perturbed copies of the current best centres. Each copy gets its own Gaussian noise with sd HOP_SD. Run _solve_once and _repair on each copy and keep the copy with the largest sum of radii. Accept it only if it beats the incumbent. Use the same time budget, so each hop is a 4-way batch of local solves. Use only the seed for randomness.
backlog.title: Best-of-k perturbations per hop

backlog.spec: Scale the perturbation of each circle inversely to its current radius. Use noise sd = HOP_SD * (r_mean / r_i) clipped to [0.3, 3] times HOP_SD, applied independently to x and y. Small circles then move more, which lets them find new holes, while large circles stay mostly in place. Keep everything else in the basin-hopping loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted hop noise

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP solve on the best packing, run a sequential linear programme. At each iteration, linearise all pair-distance and wall constraints at the current centres, then solve scipy.optimize.linprog to maximise sum(r) over centre moves and radii within a trust region of size 0.01 that shrinks by half when the step is rejected. Accept a step only if the exact sum of radii after repair improves. Run at most 30 iterations, then pass the result to _repair.
backlog.title: Sequential LP polish of radii

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a jamming-style continuation for each start. Set a common radius R, starting at 0.6 of the relaxed value. Minimise the overlap energy with L-BFGS-B. Then increase R by a factor of 1.01 each step while the energy stays below 1e-10, and cut the step to 1.001 when it does not. Use the final centres and per-circle radii, capped by the wall distances, as the SLSQP starting point. Keep the restart and hop phases the same.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-style growth continuation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, pick a random subset of k = max(2, n//8) circles, chosen with rng, and place their centres uniformly at random in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Keep the other centres at their current incumbent values. Run _solve_once on the full configuration, then clip and _repair. Accept the result only if its sum beats the incumbent. Use a fresh subset each hop.
backlog.title: Subset re-randomisation hop

backlog.spec: Every 10 hops, apply a random element of the 8-element symmetry group of the unit square to the incumbent centres, meaning reflections and 90-degree rotations, and reflect the radii with them. Then add Gaussian noise with sd 0.01 and run _solve_once and _repair. Keep the result if it beats the incumbent. This keeps the basin-hopping pool diverse without changing the restart phase. Use only the seed for randomness.
backlog.title: Dihedral-symmetry restart seeding from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the random-restart phase with a population search. Keep a population of 16 centre configurations (n x 2 arrays, drawn uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]) scored by _relax energy. For each generation, build a trial vector per member as a + F*(b - c) with three distinct random members and F=0.6, apply binomial crossover per circle with CR=0.9, clip to [0,1], run the cheap _relax on the trial, and keep it if its energy beats the member's. Every 10 generations, take the 3 lowest-energy members, run _solve_once, _repair them, and update best if the radius sum improves. Stop at the same time budget as before. All randomness comes from rng.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Exploit that 32 = 8 x 4. Add a restart mode that parametrises the packing by 8 orbit representatives (centres in the lower-left quadrant, with radii shared within each orbit). Map each representative to its four rotations by 90 degrees about (0.5, 0.5), giving 32 centres and 32 radii. Optimise the 16 centre and 8 radius variables with SLSQP, using the same non-overlap and wall constraints evaluated on the full expanded packing (or on the 8 representatives plus their images). Use this mode for about a third of the restarts. Take the best symmetric result as the seed for the existing unconstrained SLSQP polish with the full 3n variables, then run the usual repair. The unconstrained polish means the final answer is not forced to be symmetric.
backlog.title: C4-symmetric reduced search for 32 circles

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve, run a staged schedule on the wall constraints. Replace the wall constraints x_i - r_i >= 0 and similar with x_i - r_i >= m, where m starts at 0.02 and is set to 0 in three stages (0.02, 0.005, 0). Each stage runs SLSQP with MAX_ITER 100 and passes its output to the next stage. The final stage is the true problem, so the repair step still validates. This gives circles room to move away from walls early, which should avoid wall-jammed local optima. Apply it to the restart solves and the basin-hopping solves alike.
backlog.title: Wall-margin continuation

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve, spread the start configuration with a few Lloyd-style iterations. Compute the Voronoi cell of each centre inside [0,1]^2 by clipping against the other centres' bisectors, approximated on a 64 x 64 grid of sample points (assign each grid point to its nearest centre with numpy argmin, then average the grid points per centre). Move each centre to the mean of its cell. Run 10 iterations, then pass the result to _solve_once. Use the same routine on the basin-hopping perturbed configuration. This is cheap, vectorised, and aims to remove clumps in the random starts.
backlog.title: Lloyd smoothing of starts before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a new basin-hopping move alongside the Gaussian one. Pick a random centre c0 and a radius rho drawn uniformly from [0.15, 0.35]. Rotate all circles whose centres lie within rho of c0 about c0 by an angle drawn from N(0, 0.3) radians. Leave the others unchanged, clip to [0,1], and call _solve_once and _repair as usual. Choose this move with probability 0.5 and the original Gaussian move otherwise. The rotation shears the packing locally, which a Gaussian hop cannot do cheaply, so it may escape jammed local arrangements.
backlog.title: Cluster rotation hop

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that cuts the packing with a random line. Draw a unit direction u at random and an offset t in [0.3, 0.7] for the projection onto u of the centres. All circles whose projection exceeds t are translated by a random vector of length 0.03 along a tangent direction of the line, which creates a shear slip along the cut. Clip to [0,1], then run _solve_once and _repair. Use this move with probability 0.3 alongside the Gaussian hop. Keep the acceptance rule unchanged: accept only if the repaired radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Half-plane shear hop

backlog.spec: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with K=4 chains at fixed temperatures T = [0, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01] in units of radius sum. Each chain holds its own current packing and its own best. Every hop step, each chain proposes a Gaussian perturbation (HOP_SD), solves, and repairs. Accept by the Metropolis rule with probability min(1, exp((new_sum - cur_sum)/T)), with T=0 meaning accept only improvements. After every 10 hop steps, attempt a swap between adjacent chains with the standard tempering acceptance. The global best is updated whenever any chain finds a better packing. This lets the cold chain exploit while the hot chains explore.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering over hop chains

backlog.spec: Start from a packing of n+1 circles instead of n. Draw centres for n+1 circles, run the usual relax-and-SLSQP pipeline for n+1 circles, and repair the result. Remove the circle with the smallest radius and keep the remaining n circles as the candidate packing. Run SLSQP once more on those n circles with the same constraints, since removing a circle frees space, then repair. Use this as one of the restart candidate types, with the others unchanged. The aim is that an overfull packing settles into a different basin than n-circle random starts do.
backlog.title: Drop-smallest from an (n+1)-circle packing

backlog.spec: Add a small reward for tight packing to the early SLSQP stage. Modify the objective to -sum(r) - lambda * sum over circles of the nearest-neighbour gap (distance to the closest other centre minus the two radii, using the current iterate as a fixed reference, recomputed at each outer iteration), with lambda = 0.01 for the first 100 SLSQP iterations and 0 afterwards. Implement this as two SLSQP calls: the first with the bonus, the second with the true objective starting from the first result. The bonus pulls circles toward contacts and may favour jammed configurations. Keep the repair step as it is.
backlog.title: Contact-count jamming bonus during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a discrete move to basin hopping. After each accepted best packing, pick two circles i and j with radii differing by more than 0.02, and swap their centres while keeping their radii attached to the original indices, so that the large radius moves to the other location. Then re-optimise with _solve_once starting from the swapped centres with the radii as initial values, and repair. Accept only if the radius sum improves. Use this move with probability 0.2 and the Gaussian hop otherwise. This tests whether reassigning the size pattern on fixed locations can escape a local optimum that continuous moves cannot reach.
backlog.title: Pair-swap of differently sized circles in the best packing

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call in _solve_once, run a short interior-point stage. Replace the hard pair and wall constraints with a log barrier -mu * sum(log(slack)) added to the objective -sum(r), using slack = distance minus radii sum for pairs and the wall distances for boundaries. Start mu at 1e-2 and divide by 10 for 4 to 5 stages, warm-starting each stage with L-BFGS-B from the previous solution and keeping r at least 1e-6. Then pass the barrier result to the existing SLSQP call as its start point. Use only the existing time budget and the same seeds, and do not change the repair step.
backlog.title: Log-barrier continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the penalty relaxation in _relax with a Riesz p-energy repulsion over the centres, sum over pairs of 1/d^p, plus a soft wall term. Minimise with L-BFGS-B while p increases through the sequence 6, 12, 24, 48, using the previous centres as the start for each p. Do this for each of the POOL random starts, then keep the KEEP lowest-energy configurations and pass them to SLSQP as before. This drives the starts toward well-spread configurations with a smooth schedule, and it uses no new packages.
backlog.title: Riesz-energy continuation for starts

backlog.spec: Add a constructive start generator as an alternative to uniform random starts. Shuffle the circle indices and sort them into a random order of target radii, drawn from a uniform distribution on [0.06, 0.2]. Place them one at a time, each at the candidate point from a fixed grid of 400 points that maximises the largest radius feasible with the already placed circles, with ties broken toward the bottom-left corner. Store the resulting centres and their radii as the start for SLSQP. Use this generator for half of the restart starts, selected by the seed, and keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Bottom-left greedy fill starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.5 perturb the incumbent by a random affine map instead of Gaussian noise. Draw a 2x2 matrix A = I + N with N entries from Normal(0, 0.03), then set the centres to (c - 0.5) @ A.T + 0.5 + small Gaussian noise with sd 0.005. Clip the result to [0.05, 0.95] before calling _solve_once. The other half of the hops keep the current Gaussian move. This tests whether global anisotropic moves reach different basins than local jitter, while leaving the rest of the search unchanged.
backlog.title: Global affine stretch hop

backlog.spec: Add a new hop move for basin hopping. For the incumbent packing, find the circle with the smallest gap, meaning the minimum of pair distance minus radii sum or wall distance minus radius. Push that circle and its nearest neighbour apart along the line joining their centres by half the gap, plus a random factor drawn from Uniform(0.5, 1.5). Then move one random additional circle chosen from the 4 nearest neighbours of that pair by a Gaussian step with sd 0.02. Use this move with probability 0.5 and the existing Gaussian hop otherwise, then run _solve_once and _repair as before.
backlog.title: Jam-push hop

backlog.spec: Run three independent basin-hopping chains, each with its own current packing and its own rng stream spawned from the seed. Each chain runs in turn for a block of about 1/3 of the hopping time, measured with process_time. Each chain accepts a new local optimum only if its radius sum does not fall below its current value. After each round, every chain adopts the global best packing as its current state with probability 0.3 and keeps its own state otherwise. The global best is updated after every local solve. The restart phase and repair step stay as they are.
backlog.title: Island model basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a compound move to basin hopping. Choose a random adjacent pair of circles in the incumbent. Remove the smaller of the two and enlarge the other to the average of the pair radii, so the pair becomes one larger circle. Then insert a new circle with radius 0.5 times the removed radius at the point of a 60 by 60 grid that is farthest from all centres and walls. Run _solve_once on the resulting configuration and then _repair. Use this move with probability 0.2 and the Gaussian hop otherwise. The idea is to change the number of effective circles while keeping the total count at n.
backlog.title: Dimer-split and hole-insert move

backlog.spec: Use a cheap inner hop loop before the expensive SLSQP solve. For each basin-hopping step, perturb the incumbent with Gaussian noise of sd HOP_SD, then minimise a smooth penalty energy over centres and radii with L-BFGS-B, where the energy is the overlap squared plus wall violations squared minus a small weight times the radii sum. Keep the result only if its radii sum after _repair beats the incumbent, then call SLSQP only on every fifth accepted candidate. This increases the number of cheap hops by an order of magnitude while keeping SLSQP as the final polish.
backlog.title: Lightweight inner loop with penalty L-BFGS hops

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed HOP_START of 0.4 with a measured split. In the first restart round, time one full _solve_once call and count how many fit into the budget. Set the restart phase to end when restart solves have used 40 percent of TIME_FRACTION times time_limit, but never stop before at least KEEP times 2 solves are completed. Use process_time for all checks. This removes the dependence on the time taken per SLSQP call, so the restart and hopping phases get the same share of the budget across machines and values of n.
backlog.title: Calibrated budget split

backlog.spec: Change the restart loop so that the order in which the KEEP starts from each pool are refined is random. After each pool is built and sorted, draw a random permutation of the KEEP selected starts using rng, and refine them in that order. If the time budget ends mid-pool, the solves that run are a random subset rather than always the lowest-energy starts. This adds a small amount of diversity without changing the cost per solve.
backlog.title: Random restart order shuffled by seed

backlog.spec: In the restart pool, call _relax with a per-start trial radius r0 drawn uniformly from [0.9, 1.3] times 0.5/sqrt(n) instead of the fixed r0. Starts from a too-small radius leave room to spread out, and starts from a too-large radius compress into different jammed basins. Keep the pool size and KEEP unchanged and draw all randomness from rng.
backlog.title: Target-radius energy relaxation for starts

backlog.spec: Build a start by placing n points on a random-offset, randomly-skewed periodic lattice on a torus, then map each point into [0.1, 0.9]^2 by the modulo-1 fold with a random global shift. Use this as one of the starts in the restart pool, alternating with the uniform random starts. Lattice spacing comes from the count n and rng, and no coordinates are hard-coded.
backlog.title: Torus-wrap lattice start folded into the square

backlog.spec: Keep the best 5 repaired packings seen during the restart phase. For each new restart round, draw centres from a Gaussian fitted per coordinate to the elite centres (mean and sd over the elite, sd floored at 0.05), clipped to [0.05, 0.95], with 30% of starts still uniform for diversity. Run _solve_once on the best KEEP of these starts as before. This is a distribution-based version of elite reuse, not a recombination.
backlog.title: Cross-entropy sampled starts from elite centres

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, draw each hop's Gaussian sd from a log-uniform distribution over [0.005, 0.1] using rng, instead of the fixed HOP_SD=0.04. Small hops refine the basin and large hops escape it, and the mix needs no adaptation rule. Keep the acceptance rule of keeping the best packing unchanged.
backlog.title: Log-uniform multi-scale hop sizes

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, alternate two blocks for a few rounds. (a) Fix centres and maximise sum(r) by scipy linprog over the radii, using pairwise linear constraints r_i + r_j <= d_ij and wall bounds from the current centres. (b) Fix radii and run SLSQP on the centres only, with the same wall and pair constraints. Stop when the sum improves by less than 1e-7 or after 4 rounds, then pass the result to _repair as before.
backlog.title: Block-coordinate alternation of radius LP and centre SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the box walls by a smooth reparametrisation: centre coordinates are c = r + (1 - 2r) * sigmoid(u) style mapping, so each centre lies strictly inside the square for any unconstrained u. Radii are kept as constrained variables with only the pairwise and r_i <= wall-distance constraints. Run SLSQP in the reduced variable set (u, r) and map back. This removes the 4n wall inequalities from SLSQP and keeps the rest of the pipeline the same.
backlog.title: Sigmoid reparametrisation of centres

backlog.spec: For each basin-hopping perturbation, first run _solve_once with maxiter 25 as a cheap screen. Run the full MAX_ITER solve only if the screened sum is within 0.01 of the incumbent sum. Otherwise discard the hop and draw another perturbation. This increases the number of hop candidates per unit of CPU time without changing the acceptance rule.
backlog.title: Hop screening with a short SLSQP pass

backlog.spec: Add an alternative hop to basin hopping that scales all centres about their centroid by a factor exp(N(0, 0.03)) drawn from rng, then adds a small Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01 before the SLSQP solve. The choice between this hop and the usual Gaussian hop is made with probability 0.3 for the scaled hop. Accept and repair as in the existing loop.
backlog.title: Inflate-deflate centroid scaling hop

backlog.spec: Maintain a set of rounded signatures of previously found local optima, for example the sorted rounded radii to 3 decimals together with the total sum rounded to 4 decimals. Skip the repair and acceptance step whenever a new hop lands on a signature already in the set, and redraw the hop instead. This forces the hops to explore new basins and avoids spending time re-finding the same packing.
backlog.title: Tabu list of visited optima in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Replace the isotropic Gaussian hop with a noise covariance that adapts to the basin. After every 20 hops, set the per-coordinate hop sd to the empirical sd of the centre displacements of the last accepted hops, floored at 0.005 and capped at 0.1. Keep the acceptance rule unchanged. This is a diagonal covariance adaptation, a step beyond a fixed or stagnation-driven step size.
backlog.title: Covariance-adapted hop noise

incumbent.description: After the first 40% of the time budget of random restarts, repeatedly perturb the best packing's centres with Gaussian noise (sd 0.04), re-run SLSQP and repair, and keep the result only if the radius sum improves.

memo: Helped: two changes. Slot 3 (pool of 20 random starts relaxed cheaply, best refined) gave -2.9308/-2.9317. Slot 8 (perturbing the best packing after the first 40% of the budget) gave -2.9375/-2.9365, now the incumbent at -2.9370, about the published ~2.9370. Nothing since has beaten it beyond noise (sd ~0.0034). Did not help: two-tier restarts (-2.9204), perturb-and-repair (-2.9204), single-pass repair (-2.9246), greedy growth (-2.9331), hex seeding (-2.9355), warm starts (-2.9356), torus lattice (-2.9356). Within noise at -2.9375: MAX_ITER 1000, analytic Jacobians, best-of-4 hops, LP polish, shear hop, dimer move, centroid scaling. Unconfirmed single runs: slot 16 mirror-symmetric starts (-2.9386), slots 34 and 35 (-2.9386 each). Slot 21 crashed. Next: replicate slots 16, 34 and 35, since a gain of 0.0015 is still within noise. Then tune slot 8's knobs (40% split, perturbation size, circles moved) and the slot 3 pool size. Avoid more repair variants and new hop moves.
